findings.title: Handle rejections from eagerly started app imports
findings.body: Every import() here starts when the registry is evaluated, but consumers await only the entry for their selected app. The other import promises have no rejection handlers. If an unused app fails to load or throws during initialization, its rejection bypasses the importing caller's error handling and can terminate the Node worker. Defer imports until requested, or explicitly handle every eagerly started promise.

findings.title: Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks
findings.body: forEach discards the promises returned by the new async callback. Errors from getCalendar, including CalendarService construction failures that previously reached the surrounding try/catch, now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. Use an awaited Promise.all with map, or an awaited for...of loop. The same regression exists in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the requestReschedule mutation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, where initialization errors now also escape the mutation's error handling.
